papers.title: CD55 organizes lipid raft-LCK signaling to potentiate NK-cell antitumor immunity.
papers.summary: NK cells upregulate CD55 via NKG2D-p65 upon tumor encounter; CD55 engages tumor CD97 in trans, aggregating lipid rafts and activating LCK as a self-sufficient activation signal. Chronic tumor exposure depletes CD55, driving dysfunction, while restoring CD55 in NK and CAR-NK cells enhances cytotoxicity, persistence, and antitumor efficacy in vivo.

papers.title: A new agent in the matrix: PINK1's expanded role in mitochondrial surveillance and regulation.
papers.summary: This review discusses PINK1 beyond canonical mitophagy. Besides partial-import degradation in healthy mitochondria and surface stabilization leading to Parkin activation upon depolarization, recent work identifies a third fate: matrix entry. PINK1's unusual transmembrane domain governs a conformational switch, suggesting mitophagy-independent regulatory roles for PINK1 inside active mitochondria.

papers.title: Indole-3-propionic acid is an endogenic agonist of hypoxia-inducible factor-1α to protect the heart against hypoxia.
papers.summary: Indole-3-propionic acid (IPA), a gut-microbiota tryptophan metabolite, drops during hypobaric hypoxia in humans and mice, correlating with cardiac injury. IPA directly binds HIF-1α at P564, blocking VHL interaction and proteasomal degradation, shifting cardiac metabolism toward glucose. Cardiomyocyte-specific HIF-1α knockout abolishes protection; IPA also protects against myocardial infarction HIF-1α-dependently.

papers.title: AMPK phosphorylation proceeds through hierarchical proteoform cascades revealed by integrated mass spectrometry.
papers.summary: Using integrated bottom-up and top-down mass spectrometry, the authors show AMPK activation proceeds through hierarchical proteoform cascades rather than binary switching. CAMKK2 phosphorylates only α1-T183, with extensive autophosphorylation following; β1-Ser24/25 plus Ser108 cophosphorylation links localization and allostery. PP1A selectively dephosphorylates the activation loop while autophosphorylation sites remain protected.

papers.title: Natural variation in SL6 determines fatty acid components and seed longevity in rice.
papers.summary: The authors clone qSL6, encoding a fatty acyl-ACP thioesterase (SL6) that regulates palmitic acid synthesis and seed longevity in rice. ABA-derived desiccation signals act via VP1 to activate SL6 transcription. An elite allele carries a virus-derived CT-rich 5'UTR motif stabilizing mRNA; manipulating SL6 improves seed longevity without agronomic penalties.

papers.title: De novo coassembly of functional chlorophyll- and carotenoid-protein complexes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.summary: Researchers reconstructed the full chlorophyll biosynthetic pathway in Saccharomyces cerevisiae using 13 heterologous genes and 3 deletions, producing chlorophyll a at 26 μg/g dry cell weight. Adding a ketocarotenoid module enabled in vivo coassembly of functional water-soluble chlorophyll protein and cyanobacterial orange carotenoid protein with native spectral and photoactive properties.

papers.title: Ultrafast Faraday rotation probe of chiral phonon-polaritons in LiNbO(3).
papers.summary: Chiral terahertz pulse pairs excited chiral phonon-polaritons in LiNbO3, producing ultrafast Faraday rotation consistent with internal magnetization of roughly 10 magnetic moments per unit cell, equivalent to an external field exceeding 10 tesla. Signal reversal with input handedness and differential chopping controls support chiral atomic motion inducing magnetization via the inverse Faraday effect.

papers.title: Glucose-TOR-PDCB signaling restricts cell-to-cell communication through callose deposition.
papers.summary: Genetic screens for plasmodesmata transport regulators revealed that glucose-TOR-ABI5 signaling controls cell-to-cell trafficking by regulating plasmodesmata-localized callose binding proteins (PDCBs), which promote callose deposition at plasmodesmata. Despite opposite transport phenotypes, ise and dse mutants diverge mainly in TOR/ABI5-regulated genes, establishing metabolic control of intercellular transport through TOR-ABI5-PDCB signaling.

papers.title: Supramolecular immunomodulatory hydrogelator potentiates CAR-T therapy with long-lasting endogenous immunity toward solid tumor eradication.
papers.summary: A supramolecular hydrogelator forms an in situ scaffold for localized CAR-T delivery co-releasing the IDO-1 inhibitor NLG919 and PD-L1-antagonistic peptide dPPA-1, remodeling the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In melanoma, metastatic breast cancer, and postoperative glioma models, single administration enhanced CAR-T infiltration, endogenous antitumor immunity, and memory, suppressing growth, metastasis, and recurrence.

papers.title: Discovery of CDK8/19 inhibitors as lead compounds for IL-6-dependent lymphoma enabled by the formal synthesis of cortistatin A.
papers.summary: Building on a formal synthesis of cortistatin A using a late-stage SmI2-mediated oxa-bridge translocation, simplified analog CA411 selectively killed the IL-6-dependent DLBCL line OCI-LY3 by disrupting autocrine IL-6-JAK2-STAT3 signaling. CA411 suppressed xenograft growth, normalized tumor vasculature, and prolonged survival, positioning CDK8/19 inhibitors as leads for cytokine-driven lymphomas.

papers.title: CTCF aligns single-cell TAD-like domain boundaries and stabilizes long-range active chromatin clusters.
papers.summary: Using HiRES to jointly profile chromatin contacts and RNA in single nuclei, CTCF depletion left TAD-like domain number and size largely intact but increased boundary variability and reduced intra-A interactions. A subset of spatially aggregated long-distance TLD assemblies enriched for highly expressed genes and super-enhancers declined, coinciding with reduced per-cell RNA output.

papers.title: Reconstitution of multistep recruitment of ULK1 to membranes in autophagy.
papers.summary: The authors reconstitute stepwise ULK1 complex recruitment to membranes during autophagy initiation. The ATG13:ATG101 heterodimer binds PI3P-effectors WIPI2/WIPI3, inserting its WF finger into membranes, promoting ATG16L1 phosphorylation, autophagy, and mitophagy. A PVP motif in ULK1's disordered region docks onto ATG13:ATG101, positioning the kinase domain; this motif is essential for ATG16L1 phosphorylation.

papers.title: Mitochondrial superoxide-induced mitohormesis is mediated by citrate and cardioprotective.
papers.summary: Transient embryonic mitochondrial superoxide stress reprograms the adult mouse heart toward greater mitochondrial biogenesis and antioxidant capacity, protecting against doxorubicin cardiotoxicity. Mechanistically, aconitase inhibition promotes citrate export; cytosolic citrate-to-acetyl-CoA conversion drives histone acetylation. Blocking citrate export abolishes protection, while ACO2 silencing or citrate supplementation recapitulates it, identifying citrate as a redox-sensitive second messenger.

papers.title: Messenger RNA delivery of a dual CD25/CD122 affinity-tuned IL-2 variant prolongs exposure and potentiates antitumor T cell immunity.
papers.summary: An IL-2 variant with reduced CD25 and enhanced CD122 binding was fused to albumin and delivered as lipid-nanoparticle mRNA (alb-IL-2var RNA-LNP), providing sustained hepatic production. It preferentially expanded CD8+ over Treg cells in mice and cynomolgus monkeys, and combined with vaccines, checkpoint inhibitors, or radiotherapy enhanced antitumor responses, including inflammatory conversion of cold tumors.

papers.title: The fitness landscape of a form II rubisco in a photosynthetic bacterium guides engineering of oxygen tolerance.
papers.summary: A growth-coupled screen in Synechocystis evaluated 15,000 variants of a form II Rubisco from Gallionella. Beneficial mutations clustered in loop 6, the dimer interface, and putative gas tunnels. Recombination plus a trained transformer model yielded variants with reduced oxygenation efficiency and, in one case, increased carboxylation turnover, providing a large dataset for Rubisco engineering benchmarks.

papers.title: Glycemic and bodyweight effects of GIPR coding variation reflect differences in surface expression and intrinsic functional impairment.
papers.summary: Analyzing 30 GIPR coding variants in cellular models and human islets, the authors show loss-of-function variants reduce GIP-induced cAMP responses, lowering BMI but raising glycemia. Many variants impair receptor surface expression via destabilization and proteasomal degradation, with molecular dynamics revealing disrupted helical interactions, informing therapeutic targeting of GIPR in diabetes and obesity.

papers.title: Activation of transposable elements is linked to a region- and cell type-specific interferon response in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: Bulk and single-nuclei RNA-seq across four human brain regions shows transposable element expression is cell type- and region-specific. Parkinson's disease brains show elevated TE expression in microglia and neurons of substantia nigra and putamen, correlating with interferon responses; hPSC-derived microglia and neurons mechanistically confirm TE-driven IFN activation, implicating TEs in PD neuroinflammation.

papers.title: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis V9 overcomes CYFRA 21-1-linked immunochemotherapy resistance in NSCLC via microbial metabolites.
papers.summary: Elevated serum CYFRA 21-1 in advanced NSCLC correlates with gut dysbiosis, Bifidobacterium animalis depletion, and reduced immunomodulatory metabolites. Adjuvant B. animalis subsp. lactis V9 improved tumor control in mice, elevating quinaldic acid and catechol. In a randomized placebo-controlled pilot (n=30), V9 was associated with higher response rate (47% vs 33%) and prolonged progression-free survival.

papers.title: Combinatorial action of regulatory systems generates colistin heteroresistance.
papers.summary: Colistin heteroresistance in Enterobacter arises from combinatorial regulatory action: the sigma factor σE is active in about 1% of cells, generating heterogeneity, but survival additionally requires PhoPQ-mediated lipid A modification. A phoPQ mutant retains heterogeneous σE expression yet loses resistance, defining a paradigm of separate heterogeneity and resistance generators.

papers.title: Functional mapping and engineering of the Sec translocon unlocked by a cell-free system.
papers.summary: ProSecCoCo is a cell-free platform inserting SecYEG into synthetic vesicles for real-time, high-throughput Sec translocon testing. Screening 300 variants in one experiment mapped over 30 functionally critical regions across three orders of magnitude, identified super-active translocation variants, and improved nanobody export, enabling Sec engineering for synthetic biology and membrane protein production.

papers.title: KRAS is required for plexiform neurofibroma formation and represents a targetable vulnerability in established tumors.
papers.summary: In an NF1 neurofibroma mouse model, genetic Kras ablation—but not Hras—markedly reduced tumor formation, MAPK activation, and rescued disrupted Remak bundles. The orally bioavailable KRAS inhibitor BI6674 reduced volume and proliferation in established plexiform neurofibromas, remodeled the immune microenvironment, and combined with MEK inhibition enhanced regression, supporting clinical KRAS inhibition in NF1.

papers.title: A MAP-SNARE interaction links cortical microtubules to the exocytic fusion machinery during auxin-dependent growth remodeling.
papers.summary: In Arabidopsis apical hook opening, the microtubule-associated protein WDL4 binds the plasma membrane Qa-SNARE SYP121 through separate domains, linking cortical microtubules to SNARE-mediated vesicle fusion. This enhances SYP121-VAMP721 interaction and PIN1 auxin-efflux carrier recycling; wdl4 or syp121 disruption impairs PIN1 accumulation and hook opening, coupling microtubules to exocytosis during auxin-dependent growth.

papers.title: Critical role for the TGF-β1/mTORC1 signaling axis in defining the transcriptional identity of CTHRC1(+) pathologic fibroblasts.
papers.summary: Using CRISPR-Cas9, the authors show over one-third of TGF-β1-regulated matrisome genes are mTORC1-controlled. TGF-β1-stimulated fibroblast transcriptomes resemble CTHRC1+ fibroblasts from pulmonary fibrosis, an overlap lost with mTORC1 inhibition. The selective mTORC1 inhibitor RMC-5552 blocks acquisition of the collagen-high CTHRC1+ phenotype in IPF and lung adenocarcinoma fibroblasts, supporting antifibrotic mTORC1 targeting.

papers.title: Sea nettle jellyfish venom targets proteoglycans to cause cell death and pain.
papers.summary: Systematic analysis of sea nettle jellyfish venom shows dose-dependent cytotoxicity blocked by dual apoptosis/necroptosis inhibition. Genome-wide CRISPR screening identified proteoglycan biosynthesis genes as top modifiers; clinically used heparin blocks cytotoxicity at physiological doses, including one hour post-exposure, and in vivo protected against venom-induced pain, hyperalgesia, and allodynia, suggesting heparin repurposing for sting treatment.

papers.title: Sequential clearance of neutrophil extracellular traps for precision therapy of sepsis.
papers.summary: A multifunctional metal-organic framework (MOF818) combines intrinsic ROS-scavenging, NET-capturing PAMAM dendrimers, and the DNA-degrading enzyme micrococcal nuclease to sequentially clear neutrophil extracellular traps. In murine sepsis it reduced cytokine storms, organ damage, and improved survival, and in ex vivo human sepsis specimens suppressed netosis and inflammatory cytokines, offering a nanotherapeutic strategy for sepsis.

papers.title: A newly established reverse genetic system for a circular RNA virus reveals new requirements for infection and its biocontrol potential.
papers.summary: The first infectious cDNA clone of an ambivirus (Fusarium graminearum ambivirus 1) reveals that ORF-A and ORF-B proteins and embedded ribozymes are indispensable for replication. Infection triggers a fungal RNAi response, suppresses fungal growth, and reduces wheat virulence, establishing a reverse genetics platform and biocontrol potential against fungal plant pathogens.

papers.title: The actomyosin cortex controls t-tubule remodeling in skeletal muscle.
papers.summary: The actomyosin cortex beneath the plasma membrane, regulated by ARPC5-containing Arp2/3 complexes, gates membrane availability during skeletal muscle T-tubule growth. ARPC5 disruption produces enlarged T-tubules, impaired excitation-contraction coupling, and locomotor defects in mice; human triadopathy patients similarly accumulate enlarged T-tubules, implicating cortical membrane control in muscle disorder pathophysiology.

papers.title: A male-biased hypothalamic circuit modulates postmating sleep suppression in mice.
papers.summary: Male mice show delayed sleep onset and reduced sleep after mating, while females are unaffected. Single-cell transcriptomics identified preoptic Rxfp1-expressing sleep-promoting neurons selectively inhibited during mating; chemogenetic activation restored sleep. Retrograde tracing revealed male-biased GABAergic inputs from the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis, whose optogenetic activation induces immediate wakefulness specifically in males.

papers.title: Aortic disease-linked mutations reveal unexpected convergent allosteric mechanisms of protein kinase G misregulation.
papers.summary: Thoracic aortic aneurysm-associated PKG I mutations at Val234, distal from catalytic and cGMP-binding sites, disrupt autoinhibition through two convergent allosteric mechanisms: biasing active conformations with increased cGMP sensitivity, and destabilizing the regulatory domain's inhibitory contacts. NMR, simulations, and assays together explain excessive basal PKG signaling driving pathologic vascular remodeling.

papers.title: Defective EV-mediated transport of SHH alters neural fate specification in EPM1 epilepsy.
papers.summary: Patient-derived EPM1 (CSTB-mutant) cerebral organoids show hyperexcitability, disrupted excitation/inhibition balance, and ventral progenitor misspecification toward dorsal identities. CSTB deficiency impairs extracellular vesicle dynamics and reduces SHH cargo: CSTB physically interacts with SHH, and its loss diminishes SHH secretion, establishing a CSTB-SHH-EV axis safeguarding ventral patterning as an EPM1 therapeutic target.

papers.title: Hijacking pre-tRNA enables LTR-retrotransposon-initiated constitutive heterochromatin formation.
papers.summary: A genome-wide RNAi screen identified a pericentric heterochromatin initiation pathway in which PUF68 binds poly-U tracts of pre-tRNA 3' trailers; the PUF68/pre-tRNA complex base-pairs with primer binding sites of nascent LTR retrotransposon transcripts, recruiting Su(var)3-9 to catalyze H3K9 trimethylation. PUF68 alone suffices for de novo heterochromatin assembly at pericentric and ectopic loci.

papers.title: Fluorescent protein ticker tape (FPTT): Multiplexed recording of transcriptional dynamics in living cells and in vivo.
papers.summary: Fluorescent protein ticker tapes (FPTTs) integrate multispectral fluorescent proteins with self-assembling fibers to record transcriptional histories. FPTTs logged reversible endogenous cFos dynamics in neurons at 3-hour resolution over 8 days; variants for NF-κB, STAT3, mTOR, NFAT, and cAMP revealed signaling cross-talk in neurons, liver injury, cell cycle oscillations, and T cell activation.

papers.title: AKT5 is a bona fide potassium channel and controls petiole growth in Arabidopsis.
papers.summary: AKT5, long functionally unassigned, is shown to be a bona fide voltage-dependent, inward-rectifying potassium channel. Structures of closed and pre-open states confirm tetrameric channel architecture. AKT5 is expressed in young petioles; its loss suppresses petiole elongation and reduces rosette biomass under crowded conditions, implicating AKT5 in competitive growth regulation in Arabidopsis.

papers.title: NOX2/NOX4-associated oxidative stress contributes to G6PD-associated metabolic remodeling and ferroptosis during mice luteolysis.
papers.journal: Redox report : communications in free radical research
papers.summary: During mouse luteolysis, luteal regression involves ACSL4 upregulation, GPX4/GSH depletion, iron accumulation, lipid peroxidation, and elevated NOX2/NOX4. Metabolic remodeling shows 6-phosphogluconate accumulation, G6PD hyperactivation, and NADPH depletion. NOX2/NOX4 knockdown or G6PD inhibition reduced oxidative stress, ferroptosis, and partially restored progesterone secretion, linking NOX-derived ROS to G6PD-driven metabolic remodeling and ferroptosis.

papers.title: Genome analysis of the glycosphingolipid-producing green alga tetraselmis sp. NKG400013.
papers.journal: DNA research : an international journal for rapid publication of reports on genes and genomes
papers.summary: A PacBio HiFi draft genome of Tetraselmis sp. NKG400013, a glycosphingolipid-accumulating green alga, spans 423.7 Mb with 74.5% repeats and 15,322 protein-coding genes. Transposable element expansion, especially LTR retrotransposons, drove genome enlargement. Functional annotation identified glycosylceramide pathway enzymes and both Δ4 and Δ8 sphingolipid desaturases, explaining its distinctive glycosphingolipid profile.

papers.title: Hypoxia-Responsive HIF-1α-Dependent RhoA Signaling Promotes Motility and Aerotaxis in Polyaneuploid PC3 Cancer Cells with Increased Nuclear Rounding.
papers.summary: Under extreme self-generated hypoxia, polyaneuploid PC3 prostate cancer cells upregulate a HIF-1α-dependent RhoA signaling axis promoting aerotaxis, a behavior predictive of metastatic intravasation. Hypoxic PACCs show elevated HIF-1α and RhoA; disrupting either attenuates aerotaxis. Hypoxic PACCs also display increased nuclear circularity and solidity, suggesting stabilized enlarged nuclei supporting aerotactic escape toward oxygen-rich vasculature.

papers.title: Mechanism of Kushen Tongguan Pill on benign prostatic hyperplasia: roles of TLR4/NF-κB pathway and macrophage M1 polarization.
papers.summary: In a testosterone-induced rat model of benign prostatic hyperplasia, Kushen Tongguan Pill reduced prostate index, histopathological damage, collagen deposition, and inflammation while lowering serum testosterone, estradiol, and DHT. Treatment suppressed the TLR4/NF-κB pathway and macrophage M1 polarization markers in prostate tissue and in LPS/IFN-γ-stimulated THP-1 macrophages, supporting anti-inflammatory mechanism-based therapy.

papers.title: Exploring the mechanism of Panax notoginseng injection in the treatment of skin wound based on network pharmacology and experimental verification.
papers.summary: Network pharmacology identified 156 Panax notoginseng targets enriched in NF-κB, MAPK, and JAK-STAT pathways, with favorable docking of ginsenosides to TNF, IL-6, and IL-10. In a rat full-thickness wound model, PN injection reduced wound area, inflammation, and modulated TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-10 temporally, supporting regulation of the inflammation-to-repair transition in skin healing.

papers.title: MARK4 enhances stress granule formation under oxidative stress and increases tau accumulation.
papers.summary: MARK4 localizes to stress granules with TIA1 and synergistically promotes stress granule formation under oxidative stress by suppressing TIA1 dimerization. Co-expression of MARK4 and TIA1 promotes tau accumulation, while knockdown of a Drosophila TIA1 ortholog suppresses tau toxicity, identifying MARK4 as a stress granule regulator linking oxidative stress to tau pathology.

papers.title: Hepatoprotective effects of cinnamic acid against carbon tetrachloride-induced liver injury in a mouse model.
papers.summary: In CCl4-induced mouse liver injury, seven-day oral cinnamic acid pretreatment improved hepatic enzymes, bilirubin, albumin, and histology, particularly at 100-200 mg/kg. Higher doses upregulated NRF2 and FOXO3 and downregulated IL-6 and TNF-α expression without significantly altering total antioxidant capacity, suggesting hepatoprotection through antioxidant-related signaling and reduced inflammatory mediator expression.

papers.title: Multifactorial mechanisms of 5-fluorouracil-induced cardiotoxicity and the cardioprotective role of gallic acid.
papers.summary: In rats, a single 5-fluorouracil dose elevated cardiac injury markers (LDH, CK-MB), oxidative stress, inflammation, ER stress, autophagy, and apoptosis-related gene expression with histopathological changes. Oral gallic acid co-treatment markedly ameliorated these biochemical, molecular, and histopathological alterations without independent effects, supporting gallic acid as a cardioprotective adjunct during 5-FU chemotherapy.

papers.title: PTBP1 at the host-virus interface: mechanistic roles in viral RNA translation, replication, and immune modulation.
papers.summary: This review summarizes polypyrimidine tract-binding protein 1 (PTBP1) roles across viral life cycles: facilitating IRES-dependent translation of enteroviruses and hepatitis C virus, stabilizing flaviviral RNA genomes and long-distance interactions, modulating coronavirus RNA metabolism, and acting both provirally and antivirally in innate immunity and stress granule biology, with discussion of host-directed antiviral drug targeting challenges.

papers.title: Spanning-tree thermostatistics of protein allostery: an exact Kirchhoff framework with application to oncogenic KRAS.
papers.summary: A statistical mechanical framework models protein allostery via spanning-tree ensembles of residue contact networks, evaluating partition functions analytically through Kirchhoff matrix determinants without stochastic sampling. Applied to oncogenic KRAS G12D, global thermodynamics remain conserved, but channel-level analysis reveals redistributed allosteric importance along the 12-61 signaling axis and distal routes, generating testable mutation-effect hypotheses.

papers.title: Non-convulsive status epilepticus revealing acute deterioration in AARS2 mutation-associated progressive leukoencephalopathy.
papers.summary: A 41-year-old woman with AARS2-related progressive leukoencephalopathy presented with subacute cognitive deterioration; EEG revealed non-convulsive status epilepticus. Antiseizure treatment improved consciousness and normalized follow-up EEG. The case highlights that NCSE should be considered during acute neurological deterioration in leukoencephalopathy patients, where it is frequently underdiagnosed and treatable.

papers.title: A frequentist test of proportional colocalization after selecting relevant genetic variants.
papers.summary: The authors propose prop-coloc-cond, a frequentist conditional test of proportional colocalization that accounts for uncertainty in genetic variant selection, complementing Bayesian enumeration colocalization tests when results are inconclusive or prior-sensitive. Requiring only summary association data, simulations and a GLP1R expression investigation demonstrate accurate type I error control and practical utility.
